scenes.tts: Two crossovers can leave the outer markers looking untouched. How can offspring reveal a chromosome that switched twice?
scenes.caption: Two crossovers can leave the outer markers looking untouched. How can offspring reveal a chromosome that switched twice?
scenes.visual: Build the film's carried 16:9 world immediately. COLOUR MAP, fixed for both films: one parental chromosome ribbon BLUE; the other GOLD; the middle marker GREEN; crossover points RED; text WHITE. Two thick ribbons fill two-thirds of the frame height, each with three large marker blocks. Animate a RED switch between the left and middle blocks, then another between the middle and right blocks. The two outer blocks finish in their original BLUE pattern while a white question appears above them. Keep a small 'schematic' label at bottom right.
scenes.narration: Two crossovers can leave the outer markers looking untouched. How can offspring reveal a chromosome that switched twice?

scenes.visual: Title 'The Marker in the Middle' fades in for two seconds above the still-moving chromosome ribbons. Red crossover marks pulse and the ribbons drift gently; the question fades beneath the title.

scenes.tts: Follow one blue chromosome and one gold chromosome. Each carries three marker blocks in the same order. A red crossover point swaps the chromosome tails. One crossover changes the outer-marker combination. A second swap can restore it.
scenes.caption: Follow one blue chromosome and one gold chromosome. Each carries three marker blocks in the same order. A red crossover point swaps the chromosome tails. One crossover changes the outer-marker combination. A second swap can restore it.
scenes.visual: Reset the two ribbons without cutting. Label only the outer blocks 'left' and 'right'. At the first RED crossover point, the right-hand ribbon tails arc and exchange; the right marker changes parental colour. At the second RED point, the tails exchange again and the right block returns to its starting colour. A small switch counter changes from one to two without showing any biological measurement.
scenes.narration: Follow one blue chromosome and one gold chromosome. Each carries three marker blocks in the same order. A red crossover point swaps the chromosome tails. One crossover changes the outer-marker combination. A second swap can restore it.

scenes.tts: Now place a green marker between the outer markers. After two swaps, the outer colours again match a parental chromosome. The green middle marker does not. It records the hidden double crossover.
scenes.caption: Now place a green marker between the outer markers. After two swaps, the outer colours again match a parental chromosome. The green middle marker does not. It records the hidden double crossover.
scenes.visual: A large GREEN block slides into the centre of both ribbons and the double switch repeats slowly. The camera tracks the ribbon from left to right. The outer blocks settle into the parental BLUE arrangement; the middle block keeps its GREEN outline but its fill flips from BLUE to GOLD, the other parental allele, and expands slightly. A bracket joins the two RED points around it.
scenes.narration: Now place a green marker between the outer markers. After two swaps, the outer colours again match a parental chromosome. The green middle marker does not. It records the hidden double crossover.

scenes.tts: Cover the middle marker, and the double-switch product looks parental. Uncover it, and the mismatch appears. The chromosome did not change between views. The third observation changed what the cross could detect.
scenes.caption: Cover the middle marker, and the double-switch product looks parental. Uncover it, and the mismatch appears. The chromosome did not change between views. The third observation changed what the cross could detect.
scenes.visual: A dark shutter labelled 'outer markers only' slides over the GREEN block; the double-switch ribbon aligns perfectly beneath a BLUE parental template. The shutter then retracts and the GREEN mismatch glows. Transform the label into 'three markers' while the chromosome continues a slow horizontal drift.
scenes.narration: Cover the middle marker, and the double-switch product looks parental. Uncover it, and the mismatch appears. The chromosome did not change between views. The third observation changed what the cross could detect.

scenes.tts: A test cross turns these chromosome patterns into offspring classes. The recessive tester contributes the same alleles every time. Therefore each offspring phenotype reports one gamete from the heterozygous parent.
scenes.caption: A test cross turns these chromosome patterns into offspring classes. The recessive tester contributes the same alleles every time. Therefore each offspring phenotype reports one gamete from the heterozygous parent.
scenes.visual: The ribbon pair shrinks left but remains visible. On the right, a simple tester card with three recessive blocks sends identical grey allele tiles into a row of offspring boxes. The changing BLUE, GOLD and GREEN gamete ribbon supplies the other tiles. Each completed offspring box transforms into a matching gamete-pattern card.
scenes.narration: A test cross turns these chromosome patterns into offspring classes. The recessive tester contributes the same alleles every time. Therefore each offspring phenotype reports one gamete from the heterozygous parent.

scenes.tts: Eight possible gametes become eight bars. The largest pair is provisionally parental, with no detected crossover. Two middle pairs represent single crossovers. The smallest pair is provisionally double crossovers. Rarity is a clue, not proof.
scenes.caption: Eight possible gametes become eight bars. The largest pair is provisionally parental, with no detected crossover. Two middle pairs represent single crossovers. The smallest pair is provisionally double crossovers. Rarity is a clue, not proof.
scenes.visual: The offspring cards flow into eight broad bars that grow to schematic heights, clearly tagged 'schematic'. The two tallest bars inherit BLUE and GOLD outlines and move together under 'parental?'. Four middle bars form two pairs under 'single crossovers'. Two shortest bars move under 'double crossovers?'. Question marks remain on the tallest and shortest labels to preserve the viability caveat.
scenes.narration: Eight possible gametes become eight bars. The largest pair is provisionally parental, with no detected crossover. Two middle pairs represent single crossovers. The smallest pair is provisionally double crossovers. Rarity is a clue, not proof.

scenes.tts: Here are two parental patterns and two rare patterns from a schematic cross. Which marker must be in the middle? Compare each rare pattern with the parental it resembles most.
scenes.caption: Here are two parental patterns and two rare patterns from a schematic cross. Which marker must be in the middle? Compare each rare pattern with the parental it resembles most.
scenes.visual: Replace the bars with four large pattern cards using markers A, B and C, deliberately different from the lesson's p, q and r problem. Write every card in the order A, B, C. Put each rare card below the closest parental card. Only marker C, written last, differs in both vertical pairs, but do not highlight it yet. Show the question 'Which marker is in the middle?' across the top.
scenes.narration: Here are two parental patterns and two rare patterns from a schematic cross. Which marker must be in the middle? Compare each rare pattern with the parental it resembles most.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Hold all four pattern cards and the question. The cards bob almost imperceptibly; BLUE and GOLD borders shimmer, while no marker is selected.

scenes.tts: Only marker C differs in each matched pair. So C belongs in the middle, even though it is written last. The changed marker decided the order, not the written order. Unequal survival could still make another class unusually small.
scenes.caption: Only marker C differs in each matched pair. So C belongs in the middle, even though it is written last. The changed marker decided the order, not the written order. Unequal survival could still make another class unusually small.
scenes.visual: Marker C on each rare card turns GREEN and pulses. The C blocks detach and slide between A and B on a large map line, so the map reads A-C-B. The question marks on 'parental?' and 'double crossovers?' remain at the frame edge. On the viability sentence, a neutral survival gauge appears beside one bar and receives a question mark, not a diagnosis.
scenes.narration: Only marker C differs in each matched pair. So C belongs in the middle, even though it is written last. The changed marker decided the order, not the written order. Unequal survival could still make another class unusually small.

scenes.tts: Move the changed marker into the centre, then rewrite every class in map order. Each single-crossover pattern now changes colour in one interval. Each double changes in both intervals. The class list has become a map.
scenes.caption: Move the changed marker into the centre, then rewrite every class in map order. Each single-crossover pattern now changes colour in one interval. Each double changes in both intervals. The class list has become a map.
scenes.visual: All eight schematic cards return and their marker blocks slide from the written A-B-C order into A-C-B map order, with C GREEN. BLUE-to-GOLD colour changes are traced across each card. Single-crossover cards feed either the left interval or right interval on a large map; double cards send one moving RED bead into each interval.
scenes.narration: Move the changed marker into the centre, then rewrite every class in map order. Each single-crossover pattern now changes colour in one interval. Each double changes in both intervals. The class list has become a map.

scenes.tts: Count each single crossover in its own interval. Count every double crossover in both intervals, because each double crossed both. Divide each interval count by the total offspring, and express it in centimorgans. The two adjacent distances then add along the map.
scenes.caption: Count each single crossover in its own interval. Count every double crossover in both intervals, because each double crossed both. Divide each interval count by the total offspring, and express it in centimorgans. The two adjacent distances then add along the map.
scenes.visual: Keep the A-C-B map large. Single-card tokens enter only their matching interval ledger. Each double-card token splits into two linked RED counters, one entering each ledger. Display the symbolic calculation 'cM = 100 × (singles + doubles) / total' beneath each interval with no worked numbers. The two interval bars then join end to end.
scenes.narration: Count each single crossover in its own interval. Count every double crossover in both intervals, because each double crossed both. Divide each interval count by the total offspring, and express it in centimorgans. The two adjacent distances then add along the map.

scenes.tts: Hide the green marker again. Both swaps restore the outer parental combination, so those doubles vanish from a two-point count. The map becomes too short. The middle marker is the witness that prevents that loss.
scenes.caption: Hide the green marker again. Both swaps restore the outer parental combination, so those doubles vanish from a two-point count. The map becomes too short. The middle marker is the witness that prevents that loss.
scenes.visual: A shutter covers marker C and its interval boundary. The paired RED counters from each double fade from the outer-marker ledger, and a schematic distance bar visibly shortens. Reopen the shutter: C glows GREEN, both counters return, and the full adjacent-interval bar is restored.
scenes.narration: Hide the green marker again. Both swaps restore the outer parental combination, so those doubles vanish from a two-point count. The map becomes too short. The middle marker is the witness that prevents that loss.

scenes.tts: This works when the classes are scorable and adjacent intervals are short. Long intervals can hide more. Rarity is a clue, not proof. Check that rare classes survive and form a reciprocal pair. A middle marker makes double crossovers visible.
scenes.caption: This works when the classes are scorable and adjacent intervals are short. Long intervals can hide more. Rarity is a clue, not proof. Check that rare classes survive and form a reciprocal pair. A middle marker makes double crossovers visible.
scenes.visual: Return to the full BLUE and GOLD chromosome world. A small checklist appears one item at a time: 'scorable classes', 'short intervals', 'rare pair reciprocal and viable'. Each item remains secondary while the GREEN middle marker grows to the centre and the two RED crossover points pulse on either side.
scenes.narration: This works when the classes are scorable and adjacent intervals are short. Long intervals can hide more. Rarity is a clue, not proof. Check that rare classes survive and form a reciprocal pair. A middle marker makes double crossovers visible.

scenes.visual: End card over dimmed, gently drifting BLUE and GOLD ribbons. Show one centred line only: 'A middle marker makes double crossovers visible.' No title, logo, URL, or smaller line.
